clue.text: I put on soap showing spot of bother after husband is seen in bar

indicators.note: the word for a spot of bother comes after the first part of the answer
the letter for husband sits inside the word for bar, as if seen within it

parts.note: saving, as a preposition, means except or bar (all saving one)
a brush is a brief unpleasant encounter, as in a brush with the law

explanation.surface: A husband drinking in a pub runs into some minor trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub, but it is the preposition meaning except. The definition is the object's own playful description of its job.
explanation.definitionFit: This toiletry item is what a man uses to lather soap onto his face before a wet shave.

clue.text: Just about name two causes of bubbles rising in drink

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the whole assembled run is read from the bottom up, so backwards
about means around, so the bubble-makers go around the letter for name

parts.note: air and gas are the two things that form bubbles in a liquid

explanation.surface: A remark about the bubbles fizzing up in a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just about' puts the N between the two gases, and 'rising' turns the whole run upward, so AIRGNAS reads back as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish wine punch with fruit, so it is a kind of drink.

clue.text: A way in which land might be touching

parts.note: to land something is to gain or win it, as in landing a contract
ST, short for street, is a common crossword abbreviation for a way

explanation.surface: Someone explains how a piece of land might adjoin another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'land' looks like a noun but is the verb meaning to obtain, as in landing a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaning against a wall means touching it, so the preposition means in contact with.

clue.text: New line, say, associated with a book is clumsy

indicators.note: new suggests the word line made over into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: EG, for example, is what the word say means in a clue
NT, the New Testament, is a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: An editor describes an awkward new line linked to a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges LINE as INEL, followed by EG, A and NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inelegant lacks grace and polish, which is to say it is clumsy or awkward.

clue.text: Outburst stopped by British actor

indicators.note: the word for outburst is plugged, as a hole is stopped, by the letter for British

parts.note: a gale of laughter is an outburst

explanation.surface: A British performer's rant is interrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopped by' puts B inside GALE. Clark Gable was the Hollywood star of Gone with the Wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Clark Gable was a celebrated American film star, so an example of an actor.

clue.text: Men getting upset over lower score in a game

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men in crossword use
under as an adjective means lower, as in the under side

explanation.surface: Soldiers grumble about a lower score in a sporting match.
explanation.walkthrough: Rounders is a British bat-and-ball game like baseball, in which a full circuit of the bases scores one point.
explanation.definitionFit: In the bat-and-ball game rounders, a single run scored by completing a circuit is called by this name.

clue.text: Uplifting spirit, for instance, shown by excellent warriors

indicators.note: in a down clue, uplifting means lifting the run upward, so it reads backwards

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic spirit
as can mean for instance, as in such as
AI, from A1, means first-rate or excellent

explanation.surface: Brave fighters keep their spirits up with a stiff drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uplifting' turns RUM + AS upward, giving SAMUR, then AI is added.
explanation.definitionFit: The samurai were the hereditary military class of feudal Japan, its professional warriors.

clue.text: Eager to talk over hiding gem inside hand luggage

indicators.note: the outer letters conceal the word for gem tucked inside them

parts.note: glad can mean willing or eager, as in glad to help

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned over, so the word for talk reads backwards

parts.note: to gab is to chatter or talk
a stone is a precious gem

explanation.surface: Someone keen to chat smuggles a jewel in their carry-on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the talk word backwards, and 'hiding' puts the gem between the two halves; 'inside' just reinforces the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gladstone bag is a light portmanteau opening into two halves, a kind of hand-carried case.

clue.text: Stock a range of goods given time

parts.note: a line is a range of products a shop carries
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper stocks a new product range over a long period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' looks like the shop sense, but it means ancestry here.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's stock is their family descent or ancestry, which is what this word means.

clue.text: Midlander finds main road enveloped in fog

indicators.note: the road sits wrapped inside the word for fog

parts.note: brume is a literary word for mist or fog
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A traveller finds the motorway shrouded in mist.
explanation.walkthrough: A Brummie is a native of Birmingham, in England's Midlands; the motorway number 1 is written as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brummie is someone from Birmingham, the biggest city of the English Midlands.

clue.text: Age group get piece of jewellery

parts.note: an eternity, like an age, is an endlessly long time
a ring is a group of people, as in a spy ring

explanation.surface: A generation gets its jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: An eternity ring is a band set with stones all round, given as a token of lasting love.

clue.text: Upset journalist reverting to type?

indicators.note: turning back means the abbreviation for journalist is read backwards

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is a common crossword journalist
a range can mean a class or kind, a type of thing

explanation.surface: A reporter slips back into old habits.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on the idiom reverting to type, meaning falling back into old habits.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange something is to throw it into disorder, to upset or disturb it.

clue.text: Tip an originally overlooked runner to become champion

parts.note: the end of something is its tip

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for runner is passed over and left out

parts.note: a horse is a runner in a race

explanation.surface: A racing tipster advises backing an outsider that went on to win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'champion' looks like a noun for a winner, but here it is the verb meaning to support.
explanation.definitionFit: To champion a cause is to back or support it publicly, which is what endorsing does.

clue.text: Feature of restaurant I visited

indicators.note: I went into the restaurant, so the letter sits inside its short name

parts.note: trat, short for trattoria, is an Italian restaurant

explanation.surface: Someone reviews a restaurant they went to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visited' puts I inside TRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A trait is a distinguishing characteristic or feature, as of a person's character.

clue.text: Instrument is compact one? No, after reflection

parts.note: a compact is an agreement or accord
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirror-reversed, so the word No is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an instrument is portable, then thinks again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compact' looks like an adjective about size, but it is the noun meaning agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: The accordion is a musical instrument, a hand-held bellows-driven squeezebox.

clue.text: Best advertisement for pastry

parts.note: the cream is the best part, as in the cream of the crop
a puff is a piece of exaggerated promotional praise

explanation.surface: A bakery boasts of its top-rated pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream puff is a light choux pastry filled with whipped cream.

clue.text: Unfamiliar name on board of Man City?

parts.note: something new is unfamiliar
a man is a chess piece, and the castle is a name of one such piece on the chessboard

explanation.surface: A new player's name appears on the team board at Manchester City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man City' suggests the football club; Man is a chessman, and the castle (rook) is one on the board. Newcastle is a city in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Newcastle upon Tyne is a city in north-east England, so an example of one.

clue.text: Could a contemptuous expression have been making one irritable?

parts.note: was is a past form of be, as have been is
pish is an exclamation of contempt or impatience

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a sneer made a person short-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Waspish means sharply irritable and quick to sting with words, like a wasp.

clue.text: Makes strong Queen too unloved?

parts.note: Anne was Queen of Great Britain in the early 1700s

indicators.note: with no love, meaning the O for love, a zero score in tennis, is removed

parts.note: also means too, as well

explanation.surface: A question whether a queen is also disliked.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is O because it is the zero score in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: Annealing heats and slowly cools metal or glass to toughen it, so it makes it strong.

clue.text: Fold paper in the middle to kinky tale

indicators.note: only the central letter of the word paper is taken
kinky means twisted, so the letters of tale are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper runs a racy story across its centre pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the middle' takes P from paper; 'kinky' rearranges TALE as LEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a fold of cloth pressed or stitched into place.

clue.text: Following depression, long for a sense of style

indicators.note: the word for long follows the word for depression in the answer

parts.note: a pan is a hollow or depression in the ground, as in a salt pan
to ache for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: After a bout of low spirits, someone yearns for some flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' looks like an adjective but is the verb, as in long for.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant confidence and stylish flair.

clue.text: I'll be replaced finally by good boss, an intellectual

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for I is swapped for the letter for good

parts.note: the self, or I, is the ego; the 'll belongs to will be replaced
the head is the boss of an organisation

explanation.surface: Someone resigns, to be succeeded by a good, clever manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'll be replaced' reads as a resignation, but I is the self, the ego, which has its final letter changed.
explanation.definitionFit: An egghead is an informal and slightly mocking word for a highly intellectual person.

clue.text: Dog in bad state I became attached to

parts.note: base means low or morally bad
NJ is the abbreviation for New Jersey, a US state

explanation.surface: A dog in poor condition that someone grew fond of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad state' looks like one idea, but bad gives BASE and state gives NJ.
explanation.definitionFit: The basenji is a small barkless hunting dog from central Africa.

clue.text: Girl I take out again, having lost wife Times re

indicators.note: the word for take out again goes without the letter for wife

parts.note: to renew a library book is to take it out again

explanation.surface: A man dates a girl again after his wife has left.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing 'Times re' is page noise picked up when the clue was scanned, not part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a female forename, so an example of a girl's name.

clue.text: Mass indignation about a head of department

indicators.note: the word for indignation goes around the letter A

parts.note: anger is indignation

explanation.surface: Widespread outrage over a departmental chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A inside ANGER, giving ANAGER after M.
explanation.definitionFit: A manager is the person in charge of a department, so its head.

clue.text: Face shocking one

parts.note: grim means dreadful or shocking
an ace counts as one in cards and dice

explanation.surface: Someone faces a terrible person.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimace is a twisted expression, so it is a face as in pulling a face.

clue.text: Spotted pawnbroker's article

parts.note: uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone recognises an item sitting in a pawnshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' looks like the past tense of see, but it means marked with spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotted in the sense of soiled or stained means dirty, which is what unclean means.

clue.text: Whence heretics fled in disarray?

indicators.note: disarray means disorder, so the letters of these two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A history question about the town the heretics fled from in a rout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in disarray' rearranges HERETICS FLED. Chesterfield is a market town in Derbyshire, England, famous for its twisted church spire; 'Whence' asks for a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Chesterfield is a town in Derbyshire, so it is a place from which people might flee.
